title.narrative: Provision of Emergency Food Security and Livelihood Support for Drought-Affected Pastoral Households in Hargeisa Rural District

description.narrative: ltpgtThe prolonged and recurrent drought in Northern Somalia has severely affected pastoral communities in Hargeisa Rural, where consecutive failed rainfall seasons, extreme heat, and depleted rangelands have sharply reduced livestock productivity and deepened household food insecurity. The ten targeted villages—Qori Jabley, Cali-Aadan, Qotan Dabo, Gadhka Warsame Xaad, Dhubato, Ina Higare, Dabo Jilab, Bali Mataan, Balay-Golis, and Debbis—are experiencing IPC Phase 4 (Emergency) conditions marked by critical consumption gaps, distress livestock sales, and rising vulnerabilities among women, children, older persons, and persons with disabilities. With water sources drying and humanitarian coverage declining, households require urgent life-saving support. This project provides an integrated, area-based response aligned with the SHF Reserve Allocation for Drought in Northern Somalia to stabilize food access, protect remaining livelihood assets, and strengthen community coping capacities.lt/pgtltpgtltbrgtTo address immediate food needs, the project will deliver three months of unconditional cash transfers (USD 55 per month) to 1,850 drought-affected households. These households are distributed across the 10 villages: ltbrgtThe UCT beneficiaries are distributed across the ten villages as follows: Qori Jabley (110HH), Cali-Aadan (250HH), Qotan Dabo (180HH), Gadhka Warsame Xaad (350HH), Dhubato (100HH), Ina Higare (120HH), Dabo Jilab (150HH), Bali Mataan (120HH), Balay-Golis (150HH), Debbis (320HH). Beneficiary selection prioritizes female-headed households, elderly-headed households, persons with disabilities, households with malnourished children or pregnant and lactating women, minority or marginalised groups, and households that have lost income or livestock due to the drought. Activities include transparent community-based targeting, household verification, digital cash transfers, market monitoring, and a Post-Distribution Monitoring (PDM) exercise to ensure effective, safe, and accountable delivery.lt/pgtltpgtltbrgtTo prevent further erosion of pastoral livelihoods, 2,200 households will receive 352 MT of emergency mixed livestock feed to preserve core breeding animals and sustain limited milk production. Feed allocations are: ltbrgtQori Jabley (180 HH), Cali-Aadan (300 HH), Qotan Dabo (220 HH), Gadhka Warsame Xaad (250 HH), Dhubato (100 HH), Ina Higare (200 HH), Dabo Jilab (200 HH), Bali Mataan (200 HH), Balay-Golis (200 HH), Debbis (350 HH). Feeding demonstrations will guide households on prioritizing pregnant, lactating, sick, and weakened animals. Livestock feed beneficiaries will be selected based on drought-related livestock mortality, lack of alternative feed sources, and high dependence on livestock.lt/pgtltpgtltbrgtTo address the collapse of water sources, the project will implement 190 water-trucking rotations for 1,880 households. Water allocation per village includes: ltbrgtQori Jabley (180 HH), Cali-Aadan (300 HH), Qotan Dabo (150 HH), Gadhka Warsame Xaad (300 HH), Dhubato (100 HH), Ina Higare (150 HH), Dabo Jilab (200 HH), Bali Mataan (200 HH), Balay-Golis (200 HH), Debbis (100 HH). Water trucking will prevent dehydration-related livestock losses and reduce long-distance migration that increases protection risks. Ten community sessions will promote safe water handling, sanitation, and drought-resilient management practices.lt/pgtltpgtltbrgtProtection, gender equity, and accountability are integrated across all project components. The project conducts 12 gender and PSEA awareness sessions and ltbrgt10 sessions on community awareness on Drought-Resilient Livestock Management and WASH targeting around 50 participants each , to strengthen understanding of GBV risk mitigation, safe programming, reporting mechanisms, and inclusive community participation. lt/pgtltpgtltbrgtBeneficiaries receiving livestock support will also receive water-trucking assistance, while the UCT beneficiaries will be a separate grouplt/pgt
